questions.def: Use the past simple tense for completed actions in the past.
questions.question: They ___ to the cinema last night.

questions.def: Use 'be going to' for planned future actions.
questions.question: She ___ a new car next month.

questions.def: 'He' takes 'doesn't', not 'don't' in present simple negative.
questions.question: He don't like to eat vegetables.

questions.def: 'They' is plural, so use the plural form 'are'.
questions.question: They ___ my best friends.

questions.def: Use 'never' to express that something hasn't happened.
questions.question: I have ___ seen such a beautiful sunset.

questions.def: Use '-er' for comparative adjectives with one syllable.
questions.question: She is ___ than her brother.

questions.def: Use 'is thinking of buying' or 'plans to buy' instead of 'is thinking to buy'.
questions.question: He is thinking to buy a new car next month.

questions.def: Use the present continuous tense 'are doing' for now.
questions.question: What ___ you ___ now?

questions.def: Use 'a' before consonant sounds.
questions.question: He is ___ doctor.

questions.def: Use 'haven't' with 'they' in present perfect negative.
questions.question: They ___ finished their homework yet.

questions.def: 'Ate' is the past simple form of 'eat'.
questions.question: She ___ all the cake.

questions.def: Use 'the' before superlative adjectives.
questions.question: This is ___ most interesting book I've read.

questions.def: Use 'will + base form' for future conditional sentences.
questions.question: He ___ to the party if he has time.

questions.def: 'Made' is the past simple form of 'make'.
questions.question: She ___ a cake yesterday.

questions.def: Use 'didn't' for past simple negative.
questions.question: I ___ like coffee, but now I do.

questions.def: Use 'at' after 'good' to describe skills.
questions.question: She is good ___ playing the piano.

questions.def: 'Works' is the correct present simple form for 'he'.
questions.question: He ___ in a bank.

questions.def: Use 'some' for affirmative sentences with uncountable nouns.
questions.question: We need ___ sugar for the cake.

questions.def: Use 'if' to introduce a yes/no question in reported speech.
questions.question: She asked me ___ I was happy.

questions.def: 'Know' is a stative verb. Use 'knows' instead of the continuous form.
questions.question: She is knowing the answer but won't tell.

questions.def: 'Have lived' describes a past action continuing to the present.
questions.question: They ___ in Paris for 5 years.

questions.def: Use 'any' for negative sentences with uncountable nouns.
questions.question: There isn't ___ milk in the fridge.

questions.def: 'Than' is used for comparisons.
questions.question: He is older ___ me.

questions.def: 'She' takes 'goes', not 'go' in present simple.
questions.question: She go to the school every day.

questions.def: 'Seen' is the past participle of 'see'.
questions.question: Have you ___ that movie?

questions.def: We 'do' the dishes.
questions.question: I'm going to ___ the dishes.

questions.def: 'Very' modifies adjectives.
questions.question: They are ___ friendly people.

questions.def: Use the base form of the verb with 'they'.
questions.question: They ___ TV every evening.

questions.def: Use the past simple for completed actions in the past.
questions.question: I ___ a new car last week.

questions.def: 'He' requires 'doesn't', not 'don't'.
questions.question: He don't like to eat vegetables.
